title: Zee Entertainment Shares Rally 8% After SAT Grants Conditional Relief on Fundraise
excerpt: The Securities Appellate Tribunal allowed Zee to proceed with its Rs 3,143-crore warrant issue while keeping SEBI's two-month market ban and promoter trading restrictions intact.
body:
• The Securities Appellate Tribunal granted Zee Entertainment conditional interim relief, allowing its Rs 3,143-crore warrant issue to proceed despite SEBI's two-month market access ban
  • SEBI's broader restrictions remain intact — the company is still barred from the securities market, and promoters Subhash Chandra and Punit Goenka face a one-year trading ban
  • Zee shares rallied up to 8% on the SAT ruling, with the stock closing at Rs 102.57 against a previous close of Rs 96.75

Zee Entertainment Enterprises shares surged as much as 8% on Thursday after the Securities Appellate Tribunal (SAT) granted the company conditional interim relief, allowing it to proceed with its Rs 3,143-crore fundraising plan even as SEBI's market access ban remains in force.

The SAT ruling carved out a specific exception for Zee's proposed warrant issue to a promoter group entity while keeping SEBI's broader restrictions intact. The stock closed at Rs 102.57 on the NSE, up 6% from its previous close of Rs 96.75, after touching a high of Rs 104.74 during the session.

The SEBI Order and Its Impact

The ruling follows a SEBI final order that barred Zee from accessing the securities market for two months and restrained Chairman Emeritus Subhash Chandra and Managing Director Punit Goenka from dealing in securities for one year. The regulator also imposed cumulative penalties of Rs 1.48 crore — Rs 30 lakh on Zee, Rs 60 lakh on Chandra, and Rs 58 lakh on Goenka.

The case stems from an unauthorised pledge of Zee's Hyderabad property. SEBI found that original title deeds of the property were handed over to Indiabulls Housing Finance in December 2018 as security for loans worth Rs 726 crore taken by four Essel Group entities — Gnex Projects, Vivek Infracon, Gnex Infrabuild, and Renu Realtech. The regulator determined this constituted a related-party transaction executed without prior audit committee approval, violating SEBI's Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements regulations.

"SEBI's order creates a direct legal overlay on Zee's proposed fund raise. The regulator has restrained the company from accessing the securities market for a defined period."

— Alay Razvi, Managing Partner, Accord Juris

SAT's Conditional Relief

The SAT's decision mirrors a legal precedent set in the Droneacharya Aerial Innovations v. SEBI case, where a company under regulatory debarment was permitted to proceed with a preferential share issue after the tribunal granted a carved-out exception while the appeal against the debarment was pending.

Legal experts noted that the tribunal distinguished between the broader market ban and the specific fundraising transaction. Hardeep Sachdeva, Senior Partner at AZB & Partners, had earlier observed that "shareholder approval, by itself, does not grant an unconditional right to complete a capital raise" and that every step must comply with securities law.

Zee's shareholders had approved the warrant issue at an Extraordinary General Meeting on July 31, 2026 — the same day SEBI passed its final order in the Hyderabad land case, creating an immediate legal conflict.

What It Means for Zee

The fundraise is critical for Zee's financial restructuring. The Rs 3,143-crore warrant issue to a promoter group entity is aimed at strengthening the company's balance sheet and increasing the promoter stake, which has been a persistent investor concern.

While the SAT relief clears the immediate fundraising hurdle, the underlying SEBI order and its penalties remain. Chandra and Goenka continue to face personal trading bans, and the company's broader market access restrictions are still in effect for the remaining duration of the two-month ban. Zee has said it is evaluating all legal options to challenge the SEBI findings.
